messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I am trying to use stitch to impute missing genotypes, but keep receiving an error that causes termination (see below). The examples with mouse work correctly and the case of K=4 and nGens=100 work with my data, but trying K=10 and nGens=4000 errors. There may be a spot in between the 2 values that works as well but the runtimes are quite long for my data (6-7hours). Is there an option to restart the program from previous input files?
thanks,
scott

I am releasing v1.3.4, which includes faster read processing by reformatting the reads as they are streamed versus loading them all at once. Below are benchmarks for how long processing a small region from the CFW mouse population takes for each of a few versions of STITCH. Speed changes in different settings (higher coverage, K, etc.) may vary

https://github.com/rwdavies/STITCH

Best,

Robbie

messages.subject: v1.3.5 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am releasing v1.3.5, which includes more robust directory checking, failing if STITCH is unable to initialize required directories, and printing better error messages. Also, I've slightly changed the downsample procedure, to require that for each sample for each SNP specified in the pos file, that coverage is no greater than downsampleToCov. This replaces the previous behaviour of requiring that the number of reads having a "lead SNP" at each site be no greater than downsampleToCov. This should reduce the likelihood of an underflow error blowing up the math and the program. This may lead to more printings of

[1] "WARNING - downsample sample Q_CFW-SW___39.0h_recal - 15 of 19657 reads removed "

which are generally harmless unless the number of reads removed is really high. Since downsampleToCov is set to 50, throwing away reads where coverage is >50X shouldn't really be a problem for a low coverage imputation method!

https://github.com/rwdavies/STITCH

Best,

Robbie
